newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ, Transpower agree on inter-island power link.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ, Transpower agree on inter-island power link.

text.p: Electricity Corp of New Zealand (ECNZ) said on Tuesday it had reached agreement with Transpower on key terms and conditions, including payment, for Transpower's electricity transmission service between the South and North Islands.
"In respect of the inter-island link we have reached a risk-sharing agreement," ECNZ and Transpower said in a joint statement.
ECNZ and Transpower are both government owned.
ECNZ is New Zealand's largest electricity generator and Transpower is the national grid operator.
Last year Transpower announced a new pricing regime, including the proposal to charge the full cost of the power link between the two islands to the South Island generators.
ECNZ refused to comply with the new pricing regime and both parties entered formal discussions on ths issue in September, 1996.

"ECNZ will pay a smaller fixed charge than originally sought -- in exchange Transpower will retain the expected transmission rentals created by the link that would otherwise have been received by ECNZ," the two companies said.
"This agreement means end-use consumers will not be required to meet any additional costs of transmitting electricity on the power link between the North and South Islands."
A transmission rental is a sum of money created by the difference in energy price at either end of the link. It is paid to whoever meets the cost of transmission on a particular section of line.
Transpower said it fully expects that the transmission rentals will fluctuate from time to time but will meet the balance of costs for the link over the term of the contract.

"A Memorandum of Understanding has been signed between the parties. The terms of the contract with ECNZ will be for five years which is consistent with contracts offered to Transpower's other customers," the two firms said.

"The process the two companies have followed has enabled us to address a broad range of issues that were fundamental to establishing a long term relationship between the companies in the new market environment, they added.
